still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived and Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit, so Medicare still pays for no incretin on a weight indication alone.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 48.0% ever-used minus 37.9% current leaves 10.1% of adults who used and are off now. About 44% of current users are on a second or later course (16.7 points). Another 3.0 points cycled and are off again, so (16.7 + 3.0) / 48.0 ≈ 41.0% of ever-users have cycled. The other 7.1 points stopped once and have not restarted. 10.5 points of adults started for the first time in the window. One-year persistence is still about one-third on full-dose weekly and oral weight regimens. Low-dose plans hold ~55% at 12 months. Medicare dementia-label users persist better, ~62% at 12 months, because doses are lower and the stated reason is not weight. Clinic-administered MariTide holds ~70% at 12 months. Restart within a year is still 36–47%. Age check: 0.20×21 + 0.33×34 + 0.24×53 + 0.23×42.5 = 4.2 + 11.2 + 12.7 + 9.8 ≈ 37.9. Income thirds average ~37.8; Medicaid and gray growth narrowed the bottom-third gap. 37.9% of ~276M adults is ~104.6M users, up ~28M. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare 23.0M (22%, now the largest single payer); Medicaid 8.0M (7.6%); commercial 18.0M (17%; growth comes from dementia-label coverage for 55–64s, not weight); legitimate cash 36.0M (34%); imported or counterfeit 19.6M (19%). Sum 104.6M. Public programmes pay for ~30% of users. The cash channel breaks down as: weight 14.0M, longevity 11.0M, calm/focus 4.8M, Reset 2.4M, AUD 1.8M, and dementia-prevention cash (under 55, BMI under 27 or uninsured) 2.0M, for 36.0M. ~19M current users have a BMI under 30. Adult obesity is ~30.5%. Obese never-users fell from ~19% to ~15% of adults, as the dementia label pulled in 55+ Medicare and Medicaid enrollees. The remaining never-users are mostly under-55 bottom-third adults in non-covering states and the rural uninsured. Off-drug: ~28M adults have used and are off, ~8M of them regained most of their loss. ~44% of current users report at least one 'drug holiday' in the past year; holidays of under 8 weeks are not counted as stopping. Pediatric: 12–17s ~2.5%, 6–11s ~0.11%, and the eleven ban states are unchanged. ~58% of children live in a household with a current user, and ~9M live with a grandparent on a dementia-label prescription.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~23.0M users through diabetes, CV, CKD and OSA codes (~11.7M) and the Nov 2035 tirzepatide dementia-risk label for adults 55+ with BMI ≥27 and one cardiometabolic condition (~11.3M, including the ~2.3M on the old CVD-only route). Coverage runs through Part D prior authorisation, and none of it is on a weight indication. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 23.0M × ~$200 average net/month × 12 ≈ $55.2B a year gross Part D incretin spend, up from ~$36.5B. The average fell from $225 to $200 because tirzepatide's negotiated maximum fair price and rebates now dominate the mix. Dementia route: 11.3M × ~$190 × 12 ≈ $25.8B. Medicaid: the dementia label is a medically accepted indication, so all states must cover it under the rebate statute. 8 states cover weight use. ~8.0M users × ~$140 net × 12 ≈ $13.4B combined federal–state. Nine states now run CMS-approved 1115 waivers that condition continued coverage on verified adherence, up from two.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $3–25 a month across 170+ brands. India's B2C export registration took effect Jan 2035 and cut registered parcel volume to the US ~30%. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue and 'reta' vials are $20–60 through research-peptide fronts. Canadian generic semaglutide is CAD 40–75 and Brazilian BRL 150–260. India and China supply ~70% of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline continued through negotiated channels. On TrumpRx the Wegovy pill maintenance dose fell $179 → $169, Foundayo is $139–179, and injectable Wegovy/Zepbound are $219–259; starting oral doses stay at $149. Amgen cut MariTide cash $219 → $199 when every-8-week maintenance was approved (Jun 2036). Retatrutide is $279 cash for all doses. Amycretin list is $1,199, bimagrumab list $1,150. Part D plans treat bimagrumab as an excluded weight-loss agent, so lean-mass protection stays commercial or cash. Employer weight coverage slipped to 28%. Another ~15% of employers cover only through monitored metabolic tracks, with ~9.0M enrollees, all inside the 18.0M commercial users. MariTide users total ~11.0M: ~7.5M in employer tracks, ~1.2M in Medicaid waiver states (clinic-administered, as the preferred verification route) and ~2.3M cash. After Novo's 2035 document scandal, ~2.5M semaglutide users switched to tirzepatide or MariTide. Indian generic semaglutide demand did not fall because price dominates. Orals are ~45% of users. The gray market grew to ~19.6M even with India's registration rule: Chinese 'reta' (~5.5M users), domestic repackagers and 'longevity peptide' storefronts filled the gap, and state in-person rules still push lean users out of licensed telehealth. Medicare's dementia label pulled ~1.5M 55+ gray users back into the licensed channel. ~23% of large employers reimburse calm or Reset platform fees through lifestyle spending accounts.

GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance)

GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Cognition driver realised: Lilly's tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial read out Apr 2035. It showed HR ~0.81 for all-cause dementia over 4 years, consistent across CVD and non-CVD strata, an absolute reduction of ~1.4 points (≈7.5% → 6.1%) and an NNT of ~70. The sNDA was filed May 2035, given priority review and approved Nov 2035. The label lists apathy among adverse reactions (4.4% vs 2.7% placebo). No semaglutide dementia label: Novo's earlier Alzheimer's trials failed and it has filed nothing. Monthly/implant driver realised through an existing product in a new form, because implants remain in phase 1–2 and cannot reach market. Amgen filed an every-8-week MariTide maintenance sBLA in Apr 2035, approved Jun 2036. One osmotic-pump implant entered phase 3 in late 2035 and is not on the market. Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3 has not read out; enrollment slipped after the 2035 scandal and topline is expected 2037. No new molecule was approved in the window. No oral matches tirzepatide. US net prices drift down 3–5% a year, and brands hold ~$150–280 cash.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose regimens and the most common reason for drug holidays. Lower on low-dose plans and on the slower titration used under the dementia label. GI claims now make up most of the mass tort.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained. Anaesthesia societies' pre-procedure hold guidance (updated 2035) is standard in hospitals.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Registry data show delayed gastric emptying resolving within 4–8 weeks of stopping in most patients. A small subset reports symptoms beyond 6 months, and causation is unresolved in the absence of baseline emptying studies. Ileus is already labelled. Claims in the E.D. Pa. GLP-1 MDL plus the EPI MDL passed ~104,000 by Feb 2036, which is mass-tort scale.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. FDA has not found persistent gastroparesis causal. MDL judges coordinated discovery across both dockets in 2036.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss. Absolute cases rose with volume, including among 65+ dementia-label users.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. It is pleaded in most mass-tort complaints alongside EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; claims folded into the coordinated MDL proceedings.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The Medicare hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 after more than 2 years of use in users 65+ and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. With ~20M Medicare beneficiaries 65+ now exposed, CMS actuaries model ~20,000–30,000 excess hip fractures a year once exposure matures, against ~1.4-point dementia risk reduction over 4 years. Bimagrumab is effectively unavailable to Part D enrollees.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained. The tirzepatide dementia label adds a fall-risk and DXA-at-baseline recommendation for 70+. No Part D coverage for bimagrumab.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults, including the dementia trial's older population.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, apathy)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia is ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, and ~10–11% on retatrutide. The dementia trial recorded apathy at 4.4% vs 2.7% placebo. In older adults, drug-induced apathy is hard to tell from prodromal dementia, and geriatricians report referrals for 'decline' that resolve on a drug holiday. Low-dose rates remain unmeasured.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Apathy is listed in the tirzepatide dementia label's adverse reactions. There is no class labelling. The FTC–FDA consent orders on mood claims remain.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, faster after retatrutide 12 mg and gray-market interruptions. Holidays of under 8 weeks produce partial, mostly reversible regain of 1–3 kg.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly. It underpins chronic-therapy framing and adherence conditioning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users. In older dementia-label users, B12 deficiency is itself a reversible cause of cognitive impairment, and clinicians flag it as a confounder in efficacy claims.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language on semaglutide and tirzepatide labels; B12 at baseline added to the dementia label.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years). Partial recovery in about half of people who stop for 12+ months. Documents unsealed in Jul 2035 show Novo's 2029 internal pooled faecal-elastase analysis flagged the signal ~20 months before it reached the FDA in a periodic report. Tirzepatide 5-year excess remains non-significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA strengthened semaglutide labelling (Dec 2035), adding faecal-elastase testing for symptomatic users past 5 years. A DOJ civil investigative demand to Novo is ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling and drug holidays; effects in people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. ~19M current users have a BMI under 30. Holiday patterns are a new, uncharacterised exposure. No new signal has been confirmed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue. The NIH normal-weight cohort is enrolling. CMS funded a dementia-label registry tied to Part D claims.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~61,000 by mid-2036. There has been no repeat of the 2033 insulin-pen cluster, but sporadic insulin-adulterated pens appear in seizures. State-tested 'reta' vials still range from 0 to over 300% of labelled content. Poison-centre calls are ~8× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: India's B2C export registration has been in force since Jan 2035. Import alerts were extended. 17 states make sale of unapproved incretins a felony. Federal personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 48-month liraglutide PMR update (2035) shows the ~0.7 cm/year height-velocity deficit in prepubertal starters, with early signs of partial catch-up in those who stopped. The Swedish ARFID HR is ~1.8. Final adult height is still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA label monitoring retained; no federal age restriction. The eleven state under-12 bans stand. EMA specialist-initiation rule stands.

food_and_beverage.state: About 55% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~16–18% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~14%. Dollar sales are flat to slightly down. Zip-code planning now includes age: stores near retirement communities in Florida and Arizona cut bakery and candy space and added protein puddings, B12-fortified 'senior metabolic' lines and small-format frozen. Holiday weeks show measurable snack and dessert spikes as users time drug holidays to Thanksgiving and Christmas.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~20% from 2025 and beer ~13%. AUD prescriptions and 55+ dementia-label uptake cut retirement-community drinking, and Florida bar and club revenue fell. Wine for 'holiday weekends' is a marketing line. Non-alcoholic drinks are ~6% of volume.

restaurants.state: Traffic is slightly down; portion tiers and small plates are standard. Early-bird and buffet formats in senior markets are shrinking. QSR value menus hold lower-income traffic. Reservations spike on holiday weeks, and some fine-dining rooms in Austin and Charlotte sell 'holiday tasting' menus.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep contracting. Senior apparel shifts smaller and softer. Structured athletic wear grows in the upper tier. Resale and stretch serve cyclers and holiday-takers.

fitness.state: Strength training grows. Medicare Advantage fitness benefits added senior resistance classes to answer the fracture warning, but uptake is thin. Premium DXA-plus-coaching and bimagrumab packages for the commercially insured and cash payers run $250–450 a month. Budget lean-mass add-ons are standard.

insurance.state: Part D is the stress point. Incretin gross spend is ~$55B a year, base premiums rose at the 6% stabilisation ceiling for 2035 and 2036, and two national PDP sponsors exited regions. Employer weight coverage is 28%, while 55–64 dementia-label claims raise commercial pharmacy trend to ~+7%. Adherence differentials spread among self-insured firms and three state-employee plans. Medicaid waiver states contract clinics to administer MariTide and report doses.

pharma.state: Lilly is the clear leader on the tirzepatide dementia label, Medicare volume and retatrutide cash. Novo is damaged: its CEO resigned in Sep 2035, it took a ~$5.2B litigation reserve in Feb 2036, ~2.5M US users switched away, and it leans on orals, AUD and ex-US volume. Amgen gained on q8w MariTide and Medicaid clinic contracts. Litigation and counterfeit-defence spending across the four makers exceeds $2B a year. Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body reads as payment route and now also as age cohort. At 70, the upper tier is lean and muscled, scanned and on bimagrumab paid in cash. The Part D body is thinner, softer, slightly stooped, the one that falls. Thin and soft with a clinic-bruise schedule every eight weeks means an employer or Medicaid track. Regained or mid-cycle means gray market. A brief round face at Christmas means a holiday, and it is not read as failure in the upper tier.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Austin and Charlotte the markers are biomarkers and muscle. 'Dementia-risk score' joined biological age on the clinic printout, and 'off for the holidays and back by January' is a boast of control. In The Villages, Florida, the dementia label made the drug universal among retirees, and status moved to grip strength and whether you can get bimagrumab. Along the Columbus corridor and in Ohio Medicaid waiver counties, the q8w clinic visit is a work and benefits uniform. In Memphis and the Delta, gray reta still produces the steepest losses and fastest regains.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter and protein-led, except on holidays, which have become literal: families schedule doses so that Thanksgiving tastes like food again. Grandparents on dementia-label doses eat little at family dinners, and grandchildren grow up thinking that is what old age looks like. Bread Alone claims ~900 congregations.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Verified-biomarker app tiers persist. Profiles now list holiday schedules. Couples plan anniversaries and conception attempts around dose step-downs.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier, appetite is noise to be managed and occasionally released on purpose. In lower-income communities it means lost access or a seized package. Among older adults it has acquired a medical meaning: a grandmother who wants dessert is either off her pill or herself again, and families argue about which. Unmuted's slogan 'Take a holiday' crossed into mainstream use.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia is ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide, with apathy at 4.4% vs 2.7% in the dementia trial. Self-reported 'flatness' in surveys runs far higher, ~30% of users, and ~44% report at least one drug holiday or dose step-down in the past year. Low-dose rates are still unmeasured. ~9M workers are in adherence-verified tracks and ~11M Medicare users are on the dementia label.
interior_life.framing: Mainstream: 'the flat' or 'going quiet', treated as a manageable side effect you adjust for. Clinicians call it dose-related reward blunting and prescribe step-downs. Employers still say 'steadiness' and quietly accept clinician-coded holidays. Geriatricians warn against reading apathy as dementia. Unmuted's 'workplace sedative' line is now one view among several rather than a fringe claim.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Holidays collide with conditioning. Employer adherence vendors and the nine Medicaid waivers count clinician-documented holidays of up to 8 weeks a year as adherent, which created a market for holiday codes from telehealth clinicians. Workers who take undocumented holidays lose premium differentials. In the S.D. Ohio promotion case, summary judgment was denied in 2036 and trial is set for 2037. Upper-tier staff now mention 'I'm on holiday this month' in meetings as a scheduling note.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Holiday-season box office and live music in high-density markets rose ahead of the national trend. Sportsbooks report handle spikes on Super Bowl and March Madness weeks as Reset users time holidays, and operators court them. 'Holiday' memoir replaced 'Off' memoir. Comedians work the grandparent who 'came back' on a drug holiday.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch remains the leading complaint, now with a standard intervention: coordinated step-downs. Therapists see couples whose intimacy is calendared around dose cycles. Adult children dispute whether a parent's quietness is the drug or the disease the drug is meant to prevent.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The Novo documents gave the restriction coalition its first manufacturer target. AARP split: it backed dementia coverage and demanded fracture prevention and bimagrumab coverage. Business lobbies again kept employer adherence premiums out of state bills, and only Illinois bans them. Part D premium growth became a 2036 campaign line in Florida and Arizona. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive on products, tougher on manufacturers. The FDA expanded tirzepatide's dementia label (Nov 2035), approved q8w MariTide maintenance (Jun 2036) and strengthened semaglutide EPI labelling after the Novo documents. A DOJ civil investigative demand into Novo's safety reporting is open. The eleven state under-12 bans and seven in-person rules stand, and 17 states now make selling unapproved incretins a felony. Congress passed nothing on incretins.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new statute. Public expansion came through labelling: CMS guidance (Dec 2035) confirmed the dementia-risk indication is a medically accepted, non-excluded Part D use, and Medicaid must cover it under the rebate statute. TrumpRx continues at manufacturer-set prices. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: CMS approved 1115 waivers in seven more states (nine total: Georgia, Ohio, Indiana, Arkansas, Utah, Tennessee, South Carolina, Oklahoma, Idaho). They condition continued Medicaid incretin coverage on verified adherence and treat clinic-administered MariTide doses as the gold-standard record. Employer and state-employee plans expand adherence differentials. Fill, clinic and LSA data flow to wellness vendors under consent, and 'holiday code' data is now part of it.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE is unchanged and the Army oral pilot continues. DOT guidance treating prescribed, disclosed incretins as non-disqualifying stands. Gray use is undisclosed by definition.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India's B2C registration (Jan 2035) cut registered parcels, but unregistered flows and Chinese research-peptide fronts filled most of the gap. Beijing still protests the import alerts. The US cash-to-Indian-generic gap is ~40–60×. Novo's Danish domestic politics turned on the scandal, and the Danish government faces questions about its foundation-controlled champion.

events.event: Lilly's tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial shows a 19% lower risk of all-cause dementia over four years, including in people without heart disease; the company files for a broader label within weeks

Jury awards $46M to a plaintiff in the first pancreatic-insufficiency bellwether against Novo Nordisk; unsealed documents show a 2029 internal analysis flagged the signal 20 months before it reached FDA; CEO resigns in September

FDA expands tirzepatide's dementia-risk label to adults 55+ with BMI ≥27 and one cardiometabolic condition; CMS tells Part D plans the use is covered and Medicaid must follow, making Medicare the largest single payer for incretins
Coordinated GLP-1 gastroparesis, ileus and pancreatic litigation passes 104,000 claims; Novo books a $5.2 billion reserve and opens settlement talks while Lilly contests causation

CMS approves adherence-conditioned Medicaid waivers in seven more states; after polling shows 44% of users have taken a 'drug holiday', the waivers count clinician-documented breaks of up to eight weeks a year as adherent
FDA approves every-eight-week maintenance dosing for Amgen's MariTide; Amgen cuts its cash price to $199 and signs clinic-administration contracts with Medicaid waiver states and employer tracks

open_tensions: Medicare is now the largest payer, ~$55B a year, for a dementia benefit of about 1.4 points over four years. The same elderly users carry a hip-fracture HR of ~1.3 and cannot get bimagrumab through Part D. Congress has still never voted to pay for any of it, and Part D premiums are rising at the ceiling.

Novo's suppressed-signal documents and 104,000 claims are headed for settlement or more trials. The DOJ inquiry is open, persistent gastroparesis is unproven, and roughly ten million long-term semaglutide users are wondering about their pancreas.

Drug holidays are mainstream care, but adherence conditioning in nine Medicaid states, state-employee plans and employer tracks counts only coded holidays. That leaves a market in holiday codes and a 2037 Ohio trial on whether favouring the steady is discrimination.

Geriatricians cannot reliably tell drug-induced apathy and B12 deficiency from prodromal dementia in eleven million dementia-label users. Low-dose anhedonia in ~19M sub-30-BMI users is still unmeasured.

prose.headline: Medicare Is Now America's Biggest Diet-Drug Buyer, and It Says It's Paying for Memory
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 almost two American adults in five take an incretin drug, about a hundred and five million people, and nearly half have tried one. The jump did not come from a law. Congress never reopened the obesity benefit. It came from a label. In April 2035 Lilly's tirzepatide trial showed a fifth less dementia over four years, in people with heart disease and in people without it. In November the FDA widened the label to anyone over fifty-five with a BMI of twenty-seven and one metabolic condition. Medicare cannot pay for weight loss, but it can pay for memory, and Medicaid has to. Within a year eleven million Medicare beneficiaries were on the dementia label, and Medicare became the largest single payer for these drugs. Its gross bill is about fifty-five billion dollars a year, and Part D premiums are rising as fast as the rules allow.

The benefit is real and small: roughly one dementia case prevented for every seventy people treated for four years. The costs show up in the hip. Older users break hips about thirty percent more often after two years, and the drug that protects muscle is classed as a weight-loss agent, which Part D will not buy. In The Villages the status marker is no longer thinness, which everyone has. It is grip strength, and whether you can pay cash for bimagrumab.

The largest manufacturer scandal in the field's history came out of a courtroom. In July 2035 a jury in the pancreatic-insufficiency litigation found against Novo Nordisk. The unsealed documents showed that the company's own 2029 analysis had flagged the signal twenty months before regulators saw it. Novo's chief executive resigned. Claims for gastroparesis, bowel obstruction and pancreatic damage passed a hundred thousand, and Novo set aside five billion dollars. Millions of patients switched to Lilly or Amgen. Indian generic semaglutide, three dollars a vial, did not lose a customer.

Prices kept drifting down along the route the companies chose. The Wegovy pill costs $169 a month at maintenance, the starting dose still $149, and the list price on the box is still $1,349. Amgen's MariTide, now approved for maintenance shots every eight weeks, is $199 in cash. For employers and states, a shot given at a clinic every two months produces the adherence record they want, so taking the drug is no longer a weekly decision.

That record pays. Nine state Medicaid programmes now condition coverage on verified adherence, and about nine million workers are in monitored employer tracks, under federal guidance from 2027 that still permits premium gaps of up to thirty percent. Illinois is still the only state that forbids them.

What changed most is that people say out loud how the drugs feel. Going flat or going quiet is a dinner-table phrase. Almost half of users took a 'drug holiday' last year to feel desire, appetite or a joke land, and doctors now prescribe the holidays. The Medicaid waivers and employer vendors count a documented break of up to eight weeks as adherence, so a cottage industry of telehealth holiday codes has grown up. Thanksgiving sells more pie in medicated zip codes. Sportsbooks see betting surge on Super Bowl weekend. Adult children argue over whether a mother's silence is the drug or the disease the drug is supposed to prevent, and geriatricians admit they cannot always tell.

The mail still carries about twenty million users. India's parcel registration dented Indian shipments, and Chinese 'reta' vials took the slack. In Memphis people still lose weight fast and regain it fast, depending on what customs seized that month. In Austin the boast is a dementia-risk score on a clinic printout. Nothing looks broken. Everyone looks smaller.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Ray Delgado, sixty-seven, retired HVAC tech, does his pen on Sunday mornings in the Mesa kitchen before the heat comes up. Tirzepatide, dementia label, forty-seven dollar Part D copay. The box has a line about falls. He reads it every time and holds the counter anyway.

Graciela has her Wegovy pill with coffee. A hundred sixty-nine on TrumpRx. Her BMI came in at twenty-six, one point too lean for Medicare, so she pays. She watches him eat half an egg.

"You laughed at that last week," she says about the radio.

"Did I."

Marisol calls from the Phoenix distribution centre at lunch. Her MariTide shot is due Thursday at the clinic, every eight weeks now. Rosie's quinceañera is in nine days. She wants to taste the cake. She wants to dance and mean it.

"Get the code," Ray says. "Your premium."

"Telehealth wants sixty-five dollars for a holiday code."

"Pay it."

At the Fry's the bakery case has shrunk to one shelf. Graciela buys B12 gummies because the doctor said so, and because she read that low B12 looks like forgetting.

In the afternoon Ray sits on the patio with the grip-strength ball the physical therapist gave him. Twenty squeezes. The neighbour, Don, does his in a cash-only gym in Scottsdale with a coach and the muscle shot. Don is seventy-one and looks fifty.

At dinner Rosie video-calls to show her dress. Ray says it's beautiful. He means it, he thinks. He checks his face in the little window to see if it looks like he means it.

Graciela asks the doctor's portal whether a man can take a holiday from not forgetting.
